title: Contracted Emit Reconciliation Bench & Canary
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an integration-grade benchmark and canary harness that validates constrained-decoder behavior across streaming and non-streaming flows while enforcing JSON-mode contracts. The aim is to detect regressions where partially-emitted streams, interleaved tool calls, or tokenization shifts cause schema violations or require expensive reparsing on the client. This ticket covers workload design, deterministic seeding, failure injection hooks, telemetry surfaces, and an automated canary runner that gates runtime releases.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible benchmark that exercises streaming partial-emits, tool-call interleaving, and explicit constrained-decoder settings (soft vs hard enforcement).
Synthetic corpus seeded with real production prompt patterns and edge cases (truncated arrays, unexpected enums, nested optional fields).

Canary runner that runs on canary traffic mirror and flags three classes of failures: schema-violations, decode-retries > 2, and latency regressions > 2x baseline. Alerts must be routed to #infra-slo.
End-to-end test that validates fallback behaviors (schema-relaxation, sentinel insertion, graceful NAK) and records pass/fail with traces and token-level diffs.
Dashboard in Console with per-model, per-route metrics for contract-fail-rate, median repair-latency, and repair-mode distribution.
test_plan: Build harness in runtime/integration-tests/contracted-emit with knobs for: streaming chunk size, token-drop injection, toolcall ordering, and temperature/noise levels.
Create seed corpus from anonymized production prompts (1000 samples) + generated adversarial cases (fuzzed enums, boundary-length arrays, missing required keys).
Define deterministic mutation strategies: truncation at token boundaries, insertion of rogue tokens, premature EOS, and toolcall mid-object insertion.
Run baseline across 3 model families (opt-1.3b-quant, rw-compat-7b, rw-compat-70b) and two runtimes (cuda-13.1, vulkan-compat) to capture kernel scheduling impact.
Integrate canary runner with traffic mirror (10% sample) and schedule automated nightly exhaustive runs. Failures create a GitHub issue template and attach traces.
notes: 2026-02-16: Kickoff sync — agreed to prioritize canary gating for constrained-decode hard mode before release. Action: collect seed corpus by 2/22. (Aisha)
2026-02-23: Seed corpus anonymization complete. Found high incidence of optional-nulls and nested empty arrays in customer prompts. (Marco)
2026-03-02: PoC harness emits token-level diff artifacts and a minimal repair replay; initial run flagged 12 schema-violations on rw-compat-70b due to mid-stream tool calls.
2026-03-07: Design decision: canonical repair modes = [insert-sentinel, close-object, restart-stream] — chosen to minimize client-side reparse cost. Documented tradeoffs in design doc.

2026-03-10: Canary runner prototype wired to canary mirror; two automatic rollbacks prevented after detection of a regression in schema-fence performance. Follow-up: optimize KV cache interaction with constrained decode.
implementation_steps: 1) Implement harness scaffold and mutation primitives (2 sprint days).
2) Populate seed corpus and adversarial generator (3 sprint days).
3) Add telemetry hooks in constrained-decoder to emit token-level sanity events (4 sprint days).
4) Build canary runner and Console dashboard with thresholds and auto-issue generation (3 sprint days).
5) Run cross-runtime baselines, tune repair heuristics, and document fallbacks (ongoing).
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Liu): Ensure canary thresholds are conservative at first; false positives are cheaper than false negatives for schema regressions.
Design (Sana Okoye): Add sample payloads and example repair flows to the dashboard to help SREs triage quickly.
Security (Elena Morozov): Verify seed corpus anonymization and that telemetry strips PII before upload.
Runtime (Ravi Kapoor): Need to coordinate with batching team — constrained-decode backpressure interacts with batch timers.
